dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) – longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis of the cervical cord presenting as a secondary cervical/truncal dystonia

Alternatives:
1. MOG-IgG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) – another common cause of longitudinally extensive cervical myelitis that can present with prominent dystonia
2. Intramedullary spinal cord tumour (ependymoma or astrocytoma) – can produce a long T2-hyperintense cervical cord lesion and focal dystonia
3. Idiopathic inflammatory transverse myelitis – a diagnosis of exclusion that can also produce a LETM and dystonia in the absence of systemic features
